reviews.rationale: The middleware reads the parsed Origin header and rejects CR/LF before adding it to Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Whether a raw network request can deliver an embedded CR/LF to this handler depends on the pinned Go HTTP parser path; retain unresolved until an exact transport replay settles reachability.

This pattern removes block-comment text from a locally selected CLI configuration file before JSON decoding. The inspected call establishes a parser preprocessing step but no independent security-boundary guarantee for the regex.

The expression identifies comment lines while scanning a local environment file. It controls parsing of operator-managed configuration and has no separately evidenced regex-specific security guarantee at this call site.

The pattern classifies a credential prefix as API-key mode, which changes later credential handling. The source comment documents one prefix family, but the accepted key grammar and mode-selection policy are not independently specified in this repository; do not count a proof until that contract is settled.

This captures a digest from local Docker pull output and otherwise falls back to retrieving the digest directly. It is an output parser; no attacker-controlled boundary guarantee is assigned to this regex.

This removes block comments from a file before the CLI environment-variable substitution path. The file parsing path is operator-selected configuration and the inspected call does not establish an independent regex security property.
This rewrites a trailing endpoint label only when API-key mode is active. It is endpoint compatibility formatting, with no independently specified regex boundary guarantee.
This repeats the endpoint-label rewrite in another Exchange URL accessor. The transformation is compatibility formatting; this review does not infer a security contract from the pattern alone.
This repeats the endpoint-label rewrite for the model-management service URL. The transformation is compatibility formatting; no distinct security-boundary property is established.

The source comment and unit cases define a deny-list predicate used by both organization creation and deletion. Both command paths terminate with CLI_INPUT_ERROR when it returns true, before their Exchange operation. The adopted guarantee is limited to flagging the listed underscore, comma, Go RE2 ASCII whitespace, question-mark, and apostrophe characters; it is not a complete organization-name allow-list or a claim that all other characters are safe in URL paths.

reviews.rationale: This scheme-removal expression participates in a filename assembled from URL, org, and version fields. The later code sanitizes URL-derived delimiters but leaves the other formatted fields outside that expression; exact trust and path-containment requirements need a focused replay before a contract is adopted.

The replacement scrubs selected URL characters, including slash, before constructing a dependency filename. It does not by itself prove the whole filename is a safe path because org and version are formatted separately; keep the candidate unresolved pending trust, containment, and product-path evidence.

This parses operator-supplied event-selection strings into attribute/operator/value components. It is a query parser rather than a sanitizer, and no separate security guarantee is documented for this regex.

RFC3339 parsing is attempted first; the regex then extracts a date-only prefix and converts it to midnight UTC. This is a timestamp-format compatibility fallback, not an independently evidenced security-boundary regex.

The helper comment specifies a container-name alphabet and the first regex performs the character substitution, but the final Docker-facing helper composes this with another regex and normalized service metadata. A whole-helper exact-pin product replay and separate review of all inputs are needed before counting the per-character image claim.

The helper comment specifies an alphanumeric first character, and this expression rewrites a disallowed prefix. The domain includes normalized service metadata and an instance identifier; keep the composition question unresolved until the exact helper and Docker sink are replayed.

This is the digest extraction stage in the Docker image-reference parser. The parser feeds image pull and deployment paths; the repository examples do not define a complete accepted grammar, so no safety or completeness guarantee is adopted.

This captures a possible tag and path from a Docker image reference used by pull and deployment paths. The helper comment lists examples, not a complete input grammar; preserve as unresolved pending a product-parser contract.
This fallback captures an untagged Docker image path. The outputs feed Docker operations, but no complete accepted-language contract is documented at this call site.
The regex counts processor lines in a host-local CPU information file. This is a system-information parser over local operating-system data, not an untrusted-input boundary.
The regex detects a Serial field while reading a device-local system file. It parses platform inventory data and has no independent attacker-controlled boundary guarantee.
This parses the numeric MemTotal field from a host-local proc-style file. The input is local system information and the regex is not guarding an untrusted-data sink.
This parses MemAvailable from the same host-local memory file and updates a resource estimate. No security-boundary property is established for this regex.

This removes a URL scheme before forming Exchange service IDs and cache keys. The transformation is lossy and its collisions/normalization requirements depend on the product key contract; source callers show real use, but no independent specification settles whether distinct refs may alias.

This replaces a fixed set of characters in normalized service IDs used in Exchange caches and persisted-secret matching. The transform is lossy; whether its output equivalence is safe depends on an external resource-ID contract not established by these callers.
